pages.displayedText:
Muddy stared at Splashy's picture of a child eating a cheese sandwich.

"Sandwich in. Poop out? What a waste of a sandwich!"

Splashy opened the body book wider.

"Let's follow the food through the digestive system!"

CRUNCH. CHOMP.

Teeth broke the sandwich into small pieces.

Saliva, or spit, made them soft and wet. Tiny helpers called enzymes started breaking down starch in the bread.

"Spit has a JOB?" said Muddy.

pages.displayedText:
GULP!

The soft mouthful entered the esophagus: a stretchy tube leading to the stomach.

Muscles squeezed it along.

"A sandwich squeezer!" said Muddy.

Splashy followed the tube.

"Squeeze, squeeze... where next?"

pages.displayedText:
The stomach churned the food with acid and more enzymes.

SQUELCH.

Soon it looked like thick soup.

"Mud soup!" said Muddy.

"Food soup," said Splashy. "And a special, slimy lining helps protect the stomach."

The mixture moved little by little into the small intestine.

Muddy traced the long, looping tube with his nose.

"SMALL? It goes on and on!"

"It's narrower than the large intestine," said Splashy.

The liver made bile to help digest fats. The pancreas sent more enzymes, those tiny helpers that break down food.

The small intestine mixed the food with these digestive juices.

"All that teamwork for one sandwich!" said Muddy.

pages.displayedText:
The small intestine's bumpy inner wall absorbed nutrients. That means it took in useful parts from food.

Many nutrients passed into the blood.

"Hang on!" said Muddy. "Lunch is leaving the tube!"

pages.displayedText:
Blood carried nutrients around the child's body.

The body used them for energy, growing, and repairs.

Muddy tapped the child's running legs.

"So lunch helps power PLAY!"

Splashy nodded.

"But there's still something in the tube..."

pages.displayedText:
The leftovers entered the large intestine.

Its walls absorbed more water as the leftovers moved along. The waste grew thicker and formed poop.

Muddy peered closer.

"Now THAT bit looks familiar."

pages.displayedText:
Tiny living things called bacteria helped break down some leftovers.

Some made gas.

"Pffft!" said Muddy.

Splashy looked up.

"What? I was doing the sound!"

Inside the picture, a little gas bubble drifted along.

The whole trip can take a day or more.

Poop waits in the rectum, then leaves through an opening called the anus.

PLOP.

Muddy nodded.

"The exit!"

The child washed their hands.

Muddy turned back to the sandwich.

"I've solved it! The body takes useful parts. The leftovers come out as poop."

He leaned in for one last look.

SPLAT.

"Another mystery," said Splashy. "Who put a muddy noseprint on my book?"
